pg.hub.title: Platforms
pg.hub.description: Platform generations: sockets and memory. The installed base, early adopters, the penalty for changing a socket and the interest of OEM customers in new platforms.
pg.hub.page.intro: The "Platforms" window shows the platform generations (sockets and memory), the installed base of the companies and a breakdown of the rating and contract-chance multipliers of your CPUs.
pg.hub.open.tip: Generations, the installed base and a breakdown of the multipliers of your CPUs.

pg.hub.guide.title: How it works
pg.hub.guide.base.title: Installed base
pg.hub.guide.base.body: The installed base is the CPUs of a company on a socket that buyers still use: the sales of the last {0} months with fading, contract sales count with a weight of {1}%. The base of a socket raises the rating of the CPUs on it: up to +{2}% at a share of {3}% of the whole base of the market, proportionally less at a smaller share. On a standard socket {4}% of the base of the other companies on it is added to yours, on your own socket only yours counts. For Industries the rating effects work at {5}% of the usual.
pg.hub.guide.base.example: Example: your share of the base of the market is {0}%, the bonus to the rating = +{1}% x {0} / {2} = +{3}%.
pg.hub.guide.early.title: Early transition
pg.hub.guide.early.body: There are {0} places for early adopters. Whoever ships a CPU on a new platform among the first, while the window after the launch of the generation lasts (each generation has its own, usually {3} months), gets +{1}% to the rating of the CPUs of that generation; the bonus fades over {2} months. The very first becomes the pioneer. You will learn about announcements, launches and your places from letters and notifications.
pg.hub.guide.churn.title: Changing a socket
pg.hub.guide.churn.body: If you move to a new socket while your main socket (the one with your biggest base) has been supported for less than {1} months and its base is at least {2}% of the market, the rating of the CPUs on the new socket falls: the penalty of up to -{0}% equals {0}% x (1 - age of the socket / {1}) and fades over {3} months. For example, the main socket lived {4} of {1} months: -{5}%. Your own socket on the same base and pairs of compatible sockets carry no penalty. The release window of a CPU warns you in advance.
pg.hub.guide.oem.title: OEM customers
pg.hub.guide.oem.body: In every contract for computers and consoles the customer prefers a generation of platform of its own: this is decided once, when the contract appears, and depends on how far the market has already accepted the platform. A CPU on the preferred platform or a newer one raises the chance to sign the contract by {0}%, being one generation behind lowers it by {1}%, two or more by {2}%. Contracts for calculators are not affected. A big installed base adds the loyalty of the customer: up to +{3}% at a share of {4}%. When there is no contract in the question, the average of the preferences of the market is used.
pg.hub.guide.full.title: Full platform
pg.hub.guide.full.body: When the memory of a CPU is one of the standards of the generation of its socket, the platform is full, and the chance to sign a contract is higher by another {0}%.
pg.hub.guide.full.example: For the generation {0}, for example, that is the memory {1}.

pg.hub.guide.gens.none: The list of the generations appears when the game has loaded.
